$comment: Capital facts. One pack per attribute keeps IDs unique and lets a locale or a correction ship without touching unrelated content. `value.id` is the ISO 3166-2 code of the subdivision the city sits in, and it is DOCUMENTATION — nothing reads it. It is present only where the code was confirmed at authoring time; absent means unconfirmed, never irrelevant. A wrong code is worse than no code.
subject: geography

items.$comment: Amsterdam is the capital by Article 32 of the Constitution; The Hague is the SEAT OF GOVERNMENT. Both are true and the pair is a good country-page fact — but the capital is not in dispute, so this stays quizzable. Do not 'correct' it to The Hague.

source.name: Constitution of the Netherlands, Article 32 (via English Wikipedia, “Capital of the Netherlands”)

items.$comment: CONTESTED — needs a second author's sign-off before it can be quizzed. The Swiss constitution names no capital; Bern is the Bundesstadt (federal city) and the de facto seat of government since 1848. Every atlas answers 'Bern', which is why this is tempting to just ship. Resolve it deliberately, per docs/systems/content-pipeline.md#sensitive-content.

source.name: SWI swissinfo.ch, “Why Switzerland hasn’t got a capital city”

items.$comment: Kuala Lumpur is the capital; Putrajaya is the administrative centre and seat of the federal government. Both are true and the pair is a good country-page fact — the capital itself is not in dispute, so this stays quizzable.

Dodoma is the capital; Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and holds many government offices. The move was decided in 1973 and completed over decades — settled, not contested, so this stays quizzable. Dar es Salaam is a good country-page fact.
